translations.en: 25 - 'Isa ibn al-Mustafad, al-Bajali, Abu Musa al-Adarr.

chunks.arabic_text: ذُكِرَ لَهُ رِوَايَاتُهُ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ). وَلَهُ كِتَابُ "الْوَصِيَّةِ" لَا يَثْبُتُ سَنَدُهُ. وَهُوَ فِي نَفْسِهِ ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: His narrations from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) are mentioned for him. He has a book "al-Wasiyya" whose chain is not established. He is weak in himself.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Du‘afā’* identifies ‘Īsā ibn al-Mustafād al-Bajalī as a narrator of Imam Musa al-Kāzim (AS), whose standalone work *al-Wasiyya* lacks a firmly established chain (*isnād*). His classification as weak (*da‘īf*) reflects the critical scrutiny applied to individual narrators within the Shia tradition, highlighting the distinction between the reliability of the transmitter and the authenticity of the transmitted text.
en.seo_question: Who is 'Isa ibn al-Mustafad and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْأَضْرَرُ: Al-Adarr (meaning the blind or one with eye ailment)
key_terms.مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ: Musa ibn Ja'far (Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: Al-Wasiyya (The Testament/Bequest, title of a book)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator of lesser reliability)
